text:
Jake Sanderson is doing the heavy lifting on Ottawa's blue line, and the scoresheet is only half telling it. He plays 23:26 a night, sixteen points in 19 games, fifteen of them assists, and the Senators control 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he is out there. Evolving-Hockey had him fifth among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, and he has the tools to match: top-percentile skating speed and a shot clocked near 99 mph.

The odd part is the goals. One, on 2.82 expected, and a 3.1% shooting rate against a talent range that says something closer to 7%. That is a slump in finishing, not in chances. He has also put up no shots in four of his last five games, which is the number we would watch. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net more than almost any defenseman last season.

Six assists in his last ten keeps the points coming. When the shots return, the goals usually follow.
